title: ACT ON THE APPOINTMENT OF A SPECIAL PROSECUTOR, ETC. TO ASCERTAIN THE TRUTH CONCERNING SEXUAL VIOLENCE, SECONDARY VICTIMIZATION, AND OTHER MATTERS WITHIN THE MILITARY RELATED TO THE DEATH OF SERGEANT FIRST CLASS LEE YE-RAM OF THE AIR FORCE 20TH FIGHTER WING
title_original: 공군 20전투비행단 이예람 중사 사망 사건 관련 군 내 성폭력 및 2차 피해 등의 진상규명을 위한 특별검사 임명 등에 관한 법률
full_text:
ACT ON THE APPOINTMENT OF A SPECIAL PROSECUTOR, ETC. TO ASCERTAIN THE TRUTH CONCERNING SEXUAL VIOLENCE, SECONDARY VICTIMIZATION, AND OTHER MATTERS WITHIN THE MILITARY RELATED TO THE DEATH OF SERGEANT FIRST CLASS LEE YE-RAM OF THE AIR FORCE 20TH FIGHTER WING

Article 1 (Purpose)

The purpose of this Act is to prescribe matters necessary for the appointment, duties, and other matters concerning a Special Prosecutor with an independent status to ascertain the truth concerning the cases under Article 2.

Article 2 (Cases Subject to Investigation by the Special Prosecutor)

The cases subject to investigation by the Special Prosecutor under this Act shall be limited to the following:

1. Unlawful acts, including sexual violence and the infliction of secondary victimization within the Air Force, related to the death of Sergeant First Class Lee Ye-ram (including incidents of sexual harassment and sexual violence involving Sergeant First Class Lee Ye-ram in 2019 and 2020 and unlawful acts related thereto);
2. Dereliction of duty and abuse of authority, including concealment, covering up, and attempts at persuasion within the Ministry of National Defense and Air Force Headquarters in connection with subparagraph 1, and unlawful acts related thereto (including persons involved in the cases, such as military judicial police officers, members of military prosecution units, and military legal officers, within the scope of the investigation);
3. Related cases discovered in the course of investigating the cases specified in the preceding subparagraphs.

Article 3 (Appointment of the Special Prosecutor)

(1) The Speaker of the National Assembly shall, within 3 days from the date this Act enters into force, request the President in writing to appoint one Special Prosecutor to investigate the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2.

(2) The President shall, within 3 days from the date of receiving the written request under paragraph (1), request in writing that the negotiating groups under Article 33 of the National Assembly Act recommend candidates for the appointment of one Special Prosecutor.

(3) The negotiating groups receiving the written request for the recommendation of candidates for Special Prosecutor under paragraph (2) shall receive recommendations of two attorneys each from the Minister of National Court Administration and the president of the Korean Bar Association under Article 78 of the Attorney-at-Law Act, from among attorneys who have held a position specified in Article 42 (1) 1 of the Court Organization Act for at least 15 years. The negotiating groups shall agree on two candidates for Special Prosecutor from among those attorneys and recommend them to the President in writing within 5 days from the date of receiving the request.

(4) Upon receiving the written recommendation of candidates for Special Prosecutor under paragraph (3), the President shall appoint one of the recommended candidates as Special Prosecutor within 3 days from the date of receiving the recommendation.

Article 4 (Grounds for Disqualification of the Special Prosecutor)

No person who falls under any of the following shall be appointed as Special Prosecutor:

1. A person who is not a national of the Republic of Korea;
2. A public official under Article 2 of the State Public Officials Act or Article 2 of the Local Public Officials Act;
3. A person who held a position under subparagraph 2 within one year before the date of appointment of the Special Prosecutor;
4. A person who is or has been a member of a political party;
5. A person who has registered as a candidate (including a preliminary candidate) in an election held under the Public Official Election Act;
6. A person who falls under any subparagraph of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act.

Article 5 (Political Neutrality and Independence in the Performance of Duties of the Special Prosecutor)

The Special Prosecutor shall maintain political neutrality and perform duties independently.

Article 6 (Scope of Duties and Powers of the Special Prosecutor, Etc.)

(1) The scope of duties of the Special Prosecutor shall be as follows:

1. Investigating the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2, deciding whether to institute prosecutions, and maintaining prosecutions;
2. Directing and supervising Assistant Special Prosecutors and Special Investigators appointed under Article 7 and public officials seconded from relevant agencies.

(2) The Special Prosecutor shall not act beyond the scope of the Special Prosecutor’s duties by summoning or questioning persons unrelated to the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2.

(3) Where necessary for the performance of the Special Prosecutor’s duties, the Special Prosecutor may request the heads of relevant agencies, including the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office and the National Police Agency, to cooperate with investigations by submitting materials, including investigation records and evidence, concerning cases related to those specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2, providing support for investigative activities, or otherwise assisting with investigations.

(4) Where necessary for the performance of the Special Prosecutor’s duties, the Special Prosecutor may request the heads of relevant agencies, including the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office and the National Police Agency, to second public officials under their authority and provide related support: Provided, That the number of seconded prosecutors shall not exceed 10, and the number of seconded public officials other than prosecutors shall not exceed 30.

(5) The head of a relevant agency who receives a request under paragraph (3) or (4) shall comply with the request. Where the head of a relevant agency fails to comply without justifiable grounds, the Special Prosecutor may request the authority empowered to request a resolution on disciplinary action to initiate disciplinary proceedings against the head of that agency.

(6) The provisions governing the powers of prosecutors and military prosecutors in the Criminal Procedure Act, the Prosecutors’ Office Act (excluding Article 4 (2)), the Military Court Act, and other statutes and regulations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Special Prosecutor, insofar as they are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act. <Amended on May 9, 2022>

Article 7 (Assistant Special Prosecutors and Special Investigators)

(1) The Special Prosecutor may select up to 4 candidates for Assistant Special Prosecutor from among attorneys who have held a position specified in Article 42 (1) 1 of the Court Organization Act for at least 7 years and request that the President appoint them as Assistant Special Prosecutors. In such cases, the President shall appoint them as Assistant Special Prosecutors within 3 days.

(2) Under the direction and supervision of the Special Prosecutor, Assistant Special Prosecutors shall be responsible for investigations concerning the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 and for maintaining prosecutions in cases in which prosecutions have been instituted, and shall direct and supervise Special Investigators and public officials seconded from relevant agencies.

(3) Where necessary for the performance of the Special Prosecutor’s duties, the Special Prosecutor may appoint up to 40 Special Investigators.

(4) Special Investigators shall perform the duties of judicial police officers within the scope of investigations into the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2.

(5) Article 4 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the grounds for disqualification of Assistant Special Prosecutors and Special Investigators, and Article 6 (6) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the powers of Assistant Special Prosecutors.

(6) After completing an investigation, the Special Prosecutor shall keep the personnel assisting with the Special Prosecutor’s duties, including Assistant Special Prosecutors and Special Investigators, to the minimum necessary for maintaining prosecutions.

Article 8 (Duties of Special Prosecution Personnel)

(1) The Special Prosecutor, Assistant Special Prosecutors, and Special Investigators (hereinafter referred to as “special prosecution personnel”), public officials seconded under Article 6 (4), and persons hired to assist with the Special Prosecutor’s duties shall not disclose confidential information acquired in the course of their duties, either during or after their service.

(2) Special prosecution personnel, public officials seconded under Article 6 (4), and persons hired to assist with the Special Prosecutor’s duties shall not publicly disclose or divulge details of investigations, except in the cases provided for in Article 9 (3) and (4) and Articles 11 and 12.

(3) Public officials seconded under Article 6 (4) shall not report to their agencies information acquired while performing their duties on secondment.

(4) Special prosecution personnel shall not engage in work for profit or concurrently hold any other position.

(5) The provisions governing the duties of prosecutors in the Criminal Procedure Act, the Prosecutors’ Office Act, the Military Court Act, and other statutes and regulations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Special Prosecutor and Assistant Special Prosecutors, insofar as they are not inconsistent with this Act.

Article 9 (Investigation Period, Etc.)

(1) For a period of 20 days from the date of appointment, the Special Prosecutor may make preparations necessary for the performance of duties, including securing facilities necessary for investigations and requesting the appointment of Assistant Special Prosecutors.

(2) The Special Prosecutor shall complete investigations into the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 and decide whether to institute prosecutions within 70 days from the day following the date on which the preparation period under paragraph (1) expires.

(3) Where the Special Prosecutor cannot complete an investigation within the period specified in paragraph (2) or has difficulty deciding whether to institute a prosecution, the Special Prosecutor may report the reasons to the President and, with the President’s approval, extend the investigation period by 30 days, once only.

(4) The report and request for approval under paragraph (3) shall be made no later than 3 days before the investigation period expires, and the President shall notify the Special Prosecutor whether approval is granted no later than the day before the investigation period expires.

(5) Where the Special Prosecutor fails to complete an investigation or decide whether to institute a prosecution within the investigation period, the Special Prosecutor shall transfer the case to the chief prosecutor of the competent District Prosecutors’ Office within 3 days from the date on which the investigation period expires. In such cases, Article 17 shall apply mutatis mutandis to reports on expenditures, details of activities, and other matters, but the reporting period shall be calculated from the date on which the case is transferred.

(6) The chief prosecutor of the competent District Prosecutors’ Office who receives a case under paragraph (5) shall promptly complete the investigation, decide whether to institute a prosecution, and be responsible for maintaining the prosecution in any case in which a prosecution is instituted. In such cases, Article 11 shall apply mutatis mutandis to reports on the disposition of the case.

Article 10 (Trial Period, Etc.)

(1) Trials of cases prosecuted by the Special Prosecutor shall be conducted expeditiously and given priority over other trials. Judgments shall be pronounced within 6 months from the date on which the prosecution is instituted in the first instance, and within 3 months from the date on which the judgment of the preceding instance is pronounced in each of the second and third instances.

(2) In cases under paragraph (1), the periods prescribed in Articles 361, 361-3 (1) and (3), 377, and 379 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Act shall each be 7 days.

Article 11 (Reports on the Disposition of Cases)

Where, with respect to a case specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2, the Special Prosecutor decides not to institute a prosecution, institutes a prosecution, or the judgment in the case becomes final and conclusive, the Special Prosecutor shall report that fact in writing to the President and the National Assembly within 10 days in each instance.

Article 12 (Reports to the Public on Cases)

The Special Prosecutor or an Assistant Special Prosecutor acting on the Special Prosecutor’s orders may conduct press briefings on the investigation process, excluding the facts of suspected offenses, concerning the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2, in order to guarantee the public’s right to know.

Article 13 (Remuneration, Etc.)

(1) The remuneration and treatment of the Special Prosecutor shall conform to those of a chief prosecutor of a High Prosecutors’ Office.

(2) The remuneration and treatment of Assistant Special Prosecutors shall conform to those of a chief prosecutor.

(3) The remuneration and treatment of Special Investigators shall conform to those of state public officials in special service at levels equivalent to Grades 3 through 5.

(4) The Government shall pay, from reserve funds, the expenses necessary for the performance of the duties of special prosecution personnel until the Special Prosecutor leaves office.

(5) The Special Prosecutor may request the State or public institutions to provide offices, communications facilities, and other equipment necessary for the performance of the duties of special prosecution personnel. In such cases, an institution receiving such a request shall comply unless there are justifiable grounds for not doing so.

Article 14 (Retirement, etc.)

(1) The Special Prosecutor shall not resign without justifiable grounds, and any resignation shall be made in writing.

(2) Where the Special Prosecutor dies or submits a letter of resignation under paragraph (1), the President shall notify the National Assembly thereof without delay and appoint a successor Special Prosecutor in accordance with the appointment procedures prescribed in Article 3 (2) through (4). In such cases, the successor Special Prosecutor shall succeed to the duties of the predecessor Special Prosecutor.

(3) Where a successor Special Prosecutor is appointed under paragraph (2), the investigation periods of the predecessor and successor Special Prosecutors shall be aggregated for purposes of calculating the investigation period under Article 9; however, the period from the date on which the Special Prosecutor submits a letter of resignation to the date on which the successor Special Prosecutor is appointed shall not be included in the investigation period.

(4) Special prosecution personnel shall automatically retire from office upon submitting a report under Article 11 following a decision not to institute public prosecution or after a judgment becomes final and conclusive.

Article 15 (Dismissal, etc.)

(1) The President shall not dismiss the Special Prosecutor or an Assistant Special Prosecutor except in any of the following cases:

1. Where a ground for disqualification prescribed in any subparagraph of Article 4 is discovered;
2. Where the person is found to have a physical or mental illness that makes it significantly difficult to perform duties;
3. Where the Special Prosecutor requests the President to dismiss an Assistant Special Prosecutor, deeming it necessary for the performance of duties or pursuant to Article 7 (6);
4. Where Article 8 (1) or (4) is violated;
5. Where a provision concerning the duties of prosecutors that applies mutatis mutandis to the Special Prosecutor and Assistant Special Prosecutors under Article 8 (5) is violated.

(2) Where the President dismisses the Special Prosecutor, the President shall notify the National Assembly thereof without delay and appoint a successor Special Prosecutor in accordance with the appointment procedures prescribed in Article 3 (2) through (4). In such cases, the latter part of Article 14 (2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to succession to duties, and paragraph (3) of that Article shall apply mutatis mutandis to calculation of the investigation period.

(3) Where an Assistant Special Prosecutor dies or the President dismisses an Assistant Special Prosecutor, the President shall appoint a successor Assistant Special Prosecutor without delay pursuant to Article 7 (1): Provided, That this shall not apply where an Assistant Special Prosecutor is dismissed under paragraph (1) 3 (limited to cases under Article 7 (6)).

(4) When necessary for the performance of duties, the Special Prosecutor may dismiss a Special Investigator or request the head of the agency to which a seconded public official belongs to replace that official.

Article 16 (Security of Tenure)

The Special Prosecutor and Assistant Special Prosecutors shall not be removed from office unless impeached or sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment.

Article 17 (Accounting Reports, etc.)

Where the Special Prosecutor decides not to institute public prosecution or a judgment in a prosecuted case becomes final and conclusive, the Special Prosecutor shall, within 10 days, report in writing to the President on expenditures, activities, and other relevant matters, and hand over work-related documents and other materials in the Special Prosecutor’s custody to the Prosecutor General: Provided, That where public prosecution is instituted, the Special Prosecutor shall, within 10 days, submit an interim report in writing to the President on expenditures, activities, and other relevant matters up to the date on which public prosecution was instituted.

Article 18 (Judicial Authority and Jurisdiction)

(1) Notwithstanding the provisions of the Military Court Act, the courts shall have judicial authority over cases prosecuted by the Special Prosecutor under this Act.

(2) Trials in the first instance of cases prosecuted by the Special Prosecutor under this Act shall fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of a collegiate panel of the Seoul Central District Court.

Article 19 (Objections)

(1) A person subject to investigation in any of the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2, or that person’s spouse, lineal ascendant or descendant, cohabitant, or defense counsel, may file an objection with the Seoul High Court concerning conduct outside the scope of the Special Prosecutor’s duties, including a violation of Article 6 (2).

(2) An objection under paragraph (1) shall be filed in writing stating the grounds therefor and shall be submitted through the Special Prosecutor.

(3) The Special Prosecutor receiving a written objection under paragraph (2) shall handle it as follows:

1. Where the Special Prosecutor finds the objection well-founded, the Special Prosecutor shall immediately take corrective action as requested in the objection and notify the Seoul High Court and the person filing the objection thereof in writing;
2. Where the Special Prosecutor finds the objection unfounded, the Special Prosecutor shall forward the written objection, together with a written opinion, to the Seoul High Court within 24 hours after receiving it.

(4) The Seoul High Court receiving a written objection forwarded under paragraph (3) 2 shall decide on it as follows within 48 hours after receiving it. In such cases, the court may, where necessary, examine evidence, including by inspecting investigation records:

1. Where the court finds the objection unfounded, it shall dismiss the objection;
2. Where the court finds the objection well-founded, it shall uphold the claim that the investigation challenged in the objection falls outside the scope of the Special Prosecutor’s duties.

(5) Where a decision upholding an objection is rendered under paragraph (4) 2, the Special Prosecutor shall not conduct investigative activities contrary to the purport of that decision.

(6) No appeal may be filed against a decision under paragraph (4).

(7) The filing of an objection under paragraph (1) shall not suspend the Special Prosecutor’s investigative activities.

(8) A person filing an objection under paragraph (1) may, simultaneously with or separately from the objection, apply to the Seoul High Court, in writing substantiating the grounds, for a stay of all or part of the effect of the relevant disposition or other measure, its execution, or the continuation of proceedings, and the court shall decide on the application without delay.

(9) Where the Seoul High Court renders a decision under paragraph (4) or (8), it shall notify the person filing the objection and the Special Prosecutor thereof in writing.

Article 20 (Penalty Provisions)

A person who obstructs the performance of duties of special prosecution personnel by deceptive means or force shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than five years.

Article 21 (Penalty Provisions)

(1) Any member of the special prosecution personnel, public official seconded under Article 6 (4), or person hired to assist the Special Prosecutor in the performance of duties who divulges a secret learned in the course of performing duties in violation of Article 8 (1) shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than three years, suspension of qualifications for not more than five years, or a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

(2) Any member of the special prosecution personnel, public official seconded under Article 6 (4), or person hired to assist the Special Prosecutor in the performance of duties who publicizes or divulges details of an investigation in violation of Article 8 (2) shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than three years, suspension of qualifications for not more than five years, or a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

(3) A public official seconded under Article 6 (4) who, in violation of Article 8 (3), reports to the agency to which the official belongs information acquired in the course of performing duties shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than three years, suspension of qualifications for not more than five years, or a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

Article 22 (Deeming Persons Public Officials for Purposes of Applying Penalty Provisions)

Special prosecution personnel and persons hired to assist the Special Prosecutor in the performance of duties shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions under the Criminal Act or any other Act.

ADDENDA <Act No. 18843, Apr. 26, 2022>

Article 1 (Effective Date)

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Period of Validity)

This Act shall remain effective until the date on which the Special Prosecutor retires from office pursuant to Article 14 (4): Provided, That Article 9 (6) shall remain effective until the date on which the chief prosecutor of the competent district prosecutors’ office submits a report.

Article 3 (Special Cases concerning the Effects of Expiration)

The expiration of this Act shall not affect the penalty provisions under Articles 20 through 22.

ADDENDA (Prosecutors’ Office Act) <Act No. 18861, May 9, 2022>

Article 1 (Effective Date)

This Act shall enter into force four months after the date of its promulgation.

Articles 2 and 3 Omitted.

Article 4 (Amendments to Other Acts)

(1) Omitted.

(2) The ACT ON THE APPOINTMENT OF A SPECIAL PROSECUTOR, ETC. TO ASCERTAIN THE TRUTH CONCERNING SEXUAL VIOLENCE, SECONDARY VICTIMIZATION, AND OTHER MATTERS WITHIN THE MILITARY RELATED TO THE DEATH OF SERGEANT FIRST CLASS LEE YE-RAM OF THE AIR FORCE 20TH FIGHTER WING is partially amended as follows:

In Article 6 (6), “Prosecutors’ Office Act” shall be replaced with “Prosecutors’ Office Act (excluding Article 4 (2))”.

(3) Omitted.
